output.summary: A citrus tree whose wild form evolved in a restricted region of southern China and Vietnam. Its small, flattened fruits have thin, loose, pebbly skin and separate easily into segments; most commercial strains are sweeter than the bitter ancestral mandarin.
output.edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten fresh or used in salads, desserts and main dishes; peel is used fresh, as zest, dried, or as flavouring.
